newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portucel says may raise pulp prices in May.
newsitem.headline: Portucel says may raise pulp prices in May.

text.p: Portuguese pulp producer Portucel Industrial may raise prices from the present 400 ecus per tonne in May if international stocks decline and market conditions are favourable, a spokesman said.
Two Scandanavian producers announced earlier on Monday that they were considering raising prices.
"If conditions improve in terms of stocks and in terms of programmed production halts, there could be an upward correction in prices, probably in May," the Portucel spokesman said.
Northern pulp producers usually carry out routine maintenance in the late spring.
The company had been asked to comment on the statements by Sodra of Sweden and Finland's Metsa-Botnia Oy that they might raise pulp prices in mid-April and May, respectively.

Portucel's price for white eucalyptus pulp was set at 400 ecu per tonne on April 1. This was down from the 420 ecu fixed at the end of 1996 but up from market lows of around 380 seen during the first quarter of the year, the spokeman said.
